answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them at the bottom; shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five above them; shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one on top. This makes a 10-card deck ordered I, five II, four III. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: In four-player play, a human starts at 1 score; in three-player play, at 0. In either game, each human starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in their garrison and nine troops in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker is on “the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space”; two Agents start on the Leader, the third is the Swordmaster; three troops go in the garrison, “remaining nine” in supply; “Take 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after taking it your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards remaining in hand and just revealed, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, move all cards from both Agent and Reveal turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.” Reveal Effects resolve “just-revealed cards only (not of cards played on Agent turns)”; Clean Up moves all cards in front to discard.

answers.answer: No. You must pay a destination cost immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the card played, so an Agent-turn card effect cannot provide resources for that entry cost. One card lets you choose only one Agent icon and send one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs “immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played).” “You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents.” A card with no Agent icons “may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.”

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited during the turn plus up to two from the garrison, for a maximum of five in this situation. At a non-Combat space, you do not deploy troops; recruited troops go to the garrison. Troops are recruited from your supply.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: the cube recruits a troop “from your supply” into your garrison. At a Combat space, deploy “any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more units from your garrison.” Only Combat spaces permit normal deployment.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card whenever you send an Agent. The same Spy cannot be used for both effects. Choose Gather Intelligence immediately after placing the Agent and before receiving any space or played-card effects. Recalling a Spy still requires playing a card for the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Spies: Spy Agent icon grants access to a connected space “you do not recall the Spy for this.” Infiltrate recalls a Spy to ignore another player's Agent; Gather Intelligence draws a card. You cannot recall the same Spy for both. Gather Intelligence is decided “immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects).” FAQ: recalling still requires a played card.

answers.answer: The strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window with no unit in the Conflict, because only players with at least one unit there may play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; “if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.” Combat Intrigue is for players with “at least one unit in the Conflict.”

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from playing later in the phase; the Combat Intrigue window closes once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison), and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: “You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase”; resolve after all involved players “pass consecutively.” Cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: When two players tie for first, each gets the second reward, and neither wins the Conflict or takes its card. In a three-player game, no other rewards are given. In a four-player game, if exactly two tied for first, the remaining players compete for the third reward. A player with zero strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players “each gain the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card.” With three or fewer players, no other rewards; with four and exactly two tied, remaining players compete for third. Resolve Combat: “A player with 0 strength receives no reward.”

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a Conflict card cannot be doubled. For a reward that offers 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once to gain 1 VP, or pay the cost a second time (6 spice total) to gain it a second time for 2 VP total.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “if you have one or more sandworms ... double the rewards”; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. An optional reward cost may be paid “a second time to gain it a second time”; example: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2.

answers.answer: When you win a Conflict and take its card into your supply, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card there with the same battle icon. If there is a match, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During the Endgame, the wild icon can be matched with any one of the three battle icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: upon winning and taking the card, check for another “face-up Conflict or Objective card” with the same icon; if present, you “must” flip the pair for 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon may match any of the three icons.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it below 2 and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if Influence falls below 4 and earned again upon returning to 4. The first player to 4 also takes the Alliance token and gains 1 VP tied to holding it; a higher opponent can take it, transferring that VP. Merely tying the Alliance holder at 4 does not steal it. If the holder later loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player can take the token under the FAQ ruling.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: at 2, gain 1 VP and lose it below 2; the 4-Influence track bonus is kept below 4 and earned again upon returning. First to 4 gets the Alliance and 1 VP; tying does not steal it. FAQ: if holder loses Influence after being tied, formerly tied player takes the Alliance.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. It may be pooled from multiple sources to buy one card and split from one source across multiple cards. After acquiring a card, the Row is replenished from the Imperium Deck, and you may buy the replacement immediately if you can afford it. The acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects: Persuasion can acquire cards “before, between, or after” effects. Acquiring Cards: pool multiple sources or split a source; replace missing Row cards, “so after acquiring a card you may acquire its replacement”; acquired card goes face up to discard.

answers.answer: During Makers, add 1 spice to each Maker space with no Agent; bonus spice accumulates, and an Agent visiting a Maker space takes all bonus spice there. The Shield Wall prevents sandworms from being summoned to Conflicts at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin until removed. Maker Hooks are usually a stated prerequisite, but are not universal: an effect that does not specify Hooks does not require them, and Hooks are retained rather than spent. Sandworms are placed directly in your Conflict quadrant, never in a garrison, and cannot be summoned to a Shield Wall protected Conflict.
answers.evidence: Makers: empty Maker spaces receive 1 spice, added to prior bonus; sending an Agent gains all bonus spice. Sandworms: Hooks are usually required but “not a universal prerequisite”; Shield Wall blocks protected Conflicts. A sandworm is immediately deployed to your Conflict and “can never be placed in a garrison.”

answers.answer: The Endgame is triggered at Recall at the end of a round if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare Victory Points. Rulebook resource tiebreakers are, in order: spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall checks for 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck. Scoring: first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then most VP wins; tiebreakers are “spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.”

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses 20 contracts: flip two face up and leave 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle in four additional Intrigue cards and four additional Imperium cards. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are excluded and remain in the box.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle 20 contracts, flip two face up and place the remaining 18 face down; shuffle 4 additional cards into each deck; Shaddam “is not required.” The 10 contrasting-back contracts are a separate Rise of Ix set to leave in the box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If all contracts have been taken by players, it instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes when you send an Agent to a Maker space and gain at least the contract's listed spice amount during that turn, counting all sources. An Immediate contract completes as soon as taken. An Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take a face-up contract and replace it from the bank; if all have been taken, the icon gives 2 Solari. Completing contracts defines Harvest as gaining the listed spice amount that turn including other sources, Immediate as completed upon taking, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow upon next acquiring the card.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait until a future turn to complete it; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. Once completed, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: if taking a contract involving a space where your Agent was already sent “this turn, you must wait until a future turn”; you must have had it at placement. On completion, announce, gain rewards, flip face down, and leave it in supply.

answers.answer: Standard two-player play uses one shared scoring Rival as a third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective. The two humans receive the other eligible Objectives at random; the human whose Objective shows First Player gets the marker. Turn order is First Player, Rival, then the other human. The Rival takes Agent turns and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: “Use one shared scoring Rival.” It receives the Ornithopter Objective; First Player goes to the human whose card shows it; turn order is “First Player → Rival → other human.” A Rival “never takes a Reveal turn.”

answers.answer: If the Rival reveals an occupied destination, it ignores that destination and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an empty post of its specified type if available; otherwise it ignores the placement. Either way, because it did not send an Agent, it reveals another Hagal card. It ignores normal board-space costs and effects and applies only the revealed House Hagal effects and icons. If House Hagal empties or a Reshuffle card appears, it immediately reshuffles and continues.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destinations and reveal again; when Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue. Spies and Schemes: Place Spy uses an empty specified post, or ignores placement if none exists, and “either way reveal another Hagal card.” Rival effects: ignore normal space costs/effects and apply only Hagal effects.
